label: Street's dilemma extended to epistemic reasons: realist self-application and survivors
summary: #1585, revised after the independent semantic challenge on PR #1611. Source: in the pinned Street 2006 witness, n. 2 (p. 156) and n. 57 (pp. 163–164) say she thinks the dilemma extends to realism about epistemic reasons, without argument, and that her alien-investigator reply assumes shared judgments about epistemic reasons, a complication she leaves undiscussed. Two stating claims record this. Her first horn (pp. 121–122, the Bermuda analogy) holds the realist's truths fixed and lets the judgments vary with selective pressure, then argues by a coincidence step that the actual judgments are in all likelihood off track. Analyst reconstruction, attribution deferred. A Darwinian profile for one scoped epistemic evaluative judgment separates origin fixing, tracking failure, actual inaccuracy, justified defeat (undercutting in the existing ReliabilityFrame) and global epistemic nihilism. Verified results: (1) cross-history horn (28051e37): constant correctness and a verdict varying across histories give an incorrect verdict in some scenario; the probabilistic step to actual error is not derived; its controls (641cb6d7) give a fixed-truth case with an accurate actual verdict and no within-history failure. (2) Within-history-variation variant (8be398bc), an analyst reading that is not Street's horn and that her paradigm constant-correctness realism fails: origin fixing and within-history variation of correctness give a tracking failure among scenarios with the actual history. (3) Self-application (60425b3c): under a uniform mismatch-undercuts policy, the variant's premises for the debunker's own epistemic basis, sole-basis dependence and warrant-needs-undefeated-support give lack of warrant for the debunking conclusion, reusing undercutSoleBasisPrecludesWarrant; this is self-undermining, not self-refutation. The policy also treats an actually false verdict as undercutting (the actual scenario is a history-mate), so it does not by itself separate actual inaccuracy from justified defeat. (4) History-fixed correctness with actual accuracy keeps every history-mate accurate (6e78b91c). (5) Controls (92a88754): one omission example shows origin fixing is needed; the self-application premises are jointly satisfiable with the conclusion true and thin F6 intact; a no-undercutting model with history-fixed correctness keeps warrant, which shows consistency, not that antirealism specifically secures warrant. Surviving replies to this reconstruction: constructivism and functional accounts, whose correctness is fixed by the history. Necessitarian realism is NOT a survivor: it fails the within-history premise, but it is the paradigm target of the cross-history horn and survives result 4 only if its actual verdicts are accurate, which the horn disputes. Relation-asserting supervenience realism belongs to Street's second horn, which is not formalized here. The independent-basis (alien) reply against sole-basis dependence remains open for epistemic reasons. Frontier delta: no change. Root connection: F6 is a floor item that these results neither use nor threaten; the route to the case needs the unbuilt #930 bridge from epistemic warrant to acceptance of root-route premises. Follow-up #1615 (2026-11-25). A warranted bypass report must have support actually used and adequate apart from the suspect operation. With fixed correctness and cross-history verdict variation, applying the disputed policy to the debunker’s own basis yields loss of warrant if E is the only available supporting basis and warrant requires undefeated support. Controls give a true unwarranted target, an exact policy denial, another ground despite defeat, and bare error without defeat. For supervenience realism, a fixed verdict within each factor value and accurate covering exemplars transport correctness across the represented cases. The earlier quantitative factor/truth bound remains available for fallible alignment. The blind pilot discriminated local, selective and external response rules under a fixed menu. It supplied no actual reliability or report warrant. See the #1615 section of the note for the dated prediction, committed key, reveal and interpretive limits.
blocker: Application is open. Select an actual epistemic judgment used by a debunker, identify its producing basis and a report warranted independently of that operation, then test residual cue information and possible alternative target grounds. Neither cross-history variation nor single-task accuracy supplies the reference class or transmission evidence. For the relation horn, identify a noncircular calibration panel covering the claimed factor values or justify fallible bounds on the same target subclass. The first-horn probabilistic coincidence premise and the #930 bridge to accepting particular root premises remain open. The #1980 F6 population route requires a positive reason witness and ontic representation.

current_assessment.scope: The basis-specific defeat policy for the fixed-truth cross-history horn, its reflexive application and calibrated supervenience reply (#1615).
current_assessment.assessment: A warranted process trace supports withdrawing credit for firsthand comparison. Full defeat of the producing basis requires further warrant that the cue contributes no surviving evidence. A calibrated testimonial proxy can meet the bypass and variation conditions while retaining evidential force. Warrant can survive local defeat when independent grounds adequately sustain the subject’s acceptance. If the contested policy undercuts the debunker’s own basis, that basis exhausts available support, and warrant requires undefeated support, the debunker loses warrant for that conclusion. If truth and verdict are each fixed at a given factor value, accuracy on a panel covering every represented factor value transfers to all cases in that scope. Neither actual defeat nor a moral-to-God inference has been established.
